explanation: The same article closes the other side of the link. “1966 anti-Igbo pogrom”, at revision 1376650990, lead: “These events led to the secession of the eastern Nigerian region and the declaration of Biafra, which ultimately led to the Nigerian Civil War.” § Aftermath: “It also was the precursor to Ojukwu's declaration of Eastern Nigeria's secession from the federation as the Republic of Biafra, and the resulting Nigerian Civil War (1967–1970)” And § Background, of the September killings: “It has been described as the most painful and provocative incident leading to the Nigeria-Biafra War.” The edge is `precondition-of`, which says the pogrom supplied something the war needed without causing it. The article puts the secession and the declaration of Biafra next to the war as its cause, and the atlas holds neither as a record. The pogrom is what the secession answered, one step back. The confidence is `probable` under rule 22.
